name: Cowpea Anthracnose
description: A fungal disease causing dark, sunken lesions on cowpea stems, leaves, and pods. It is seed-borne and can cause significant yield losses in humid growing conditions.
symptoms: Dark brown to black sunken lesions on stems and petioles
Leaf lesions as dark spots with reddish-brown borders
Pod lesions as circular or elongated dark sunken areas
Seedling damping off in severe seed infection
causes: Warm, humid weather favoring spore spread
Rain splash dispersing spores to healthy plants
treatments: Apply fungicides containing carbendazim or thiram
Spray chlorothalonil or mancozeb at first symptoms
Use copper-based fungicides as preventive treatment
Seed treatment with thiram or captan before planting
prevention: Treat seeds with fungicide before planting
Practice crop rotation with non-legume crops
Remove and destroy infected crop debris
Avoid dense planting to improve air circulation
